title: Define record ownership before a system handoff
intro: For semiconductor equipment-component suppliers, factory IT and operating teams need shared definitions, record responsibility and clear receiving decisions.

sections.heading: Start with one production record
paragraphs: Choose one record that planning or quality teams need. Identify its meaning, update timing and production scope.
Record which team and system maintains it, who checks differences and who confirms the handoff.

sections.heading: Separate enterprise and production responsibilities
paragraphs: ERP supports enterprise orders, materials, planning and costs. Manufacturing execution solutions support production progress, lot records and quality information.
Use these roles to discuss record responsibility and process needs. Define the technical scope with the factory teams before selecting a handoff approach.

sections.heading: Industry context: Wafer Works
paragraphs: Wafer Works / 合晶科技 in Taiwan / Shanghai produces silicon wafer materials through crystal growth, wafer processing and epitaxy.
The case connects silicon crystals to wafer-lot production history and provides visibility into progress, equipment status and epitaxy records with quality parameter limits.
These production-information topics help factory teams identify the records and responsibilities to discuss in their own processes.

sections.heading: Define the local factory scope
paragraphs: Digiwin Vietnam assesses factory operations, advises on business processes and supports on-site solution transfer and factory acceptance.
Bring one current information handoff, its record owner, receiving decision and unresolved differences to a discussion of your process and implementation scope.
